DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS (please keep this sheet)

Patient: ABERNATHY-RUIZ, Thaddeus J.   Goes by: "Tad"
MRN 00718842-RB | CSN 4402917730 | DOB 07/14/1968 | Age 58 yrs
Visit: 10/03/2026, 14:22-19:05
Treated by: Wendell Colles, MD (attending); Ji-woo Park, PA-C
Discharging nurse: Maribel Fuentes, RN

WHY YOU CAME IN
Tad, you fell about 8 feet from an extension ladder while cleaning the gutters at your home (418 Hartwell Ave, Oakwood, OH 45409). You put out your right hand to catch yourself. Your wife Joy drove you here.

WHAT WE FOUND
* Right wrist: a break in the radius bone just above the wrist, called a Colles fracture (the broken end tips toward the back of the hand). Dr. Colles numbed the area, set the bone back in line and put on a sugar-tong splint. The x-ray after splinting showed good position.
* Head CT and neck exam: normal. No other injuries found.
* Last vitals: BP 148/86, pulse 84. Pain went from 8/10 on arrival to 4/10.

WHAT TO DO AT HOME
* Keep the splint clean and DRY. Cover it with a bag to shower. Do not push anything inside it.
* Keep your hand above heart level on 2 pillows for the next 48-72 hours and wiggle your fingers often. Your fingers may look a tad puffy and bruised - that is expected.
* Ice over the splint 20 minutes at a time (keep the splint dry).
* Pain: acetaminophen (Tylenol) 1,000 mg every 8 hours, plus ibuprofen 400 mg every 6 hours with food if you have no kidney or stomach problems. A few oxycodone 5 mg tablets were prescribed for nights only - no driving or ladders while taking them.
* No climbing, no lifting over 2 lb with the right hand, and no work as a lineman until cleared. Work note for Miami Valley Power & Light given: off duty through 10-19-26.

FOLLOW-UP
Hand surgery clinic: Dr. Naledi Okonkwo-Hart, Gem City Orthopaedics, 3200 Far Hills Ave, Suite 210, Kettering, OH 45429.
Appointment: Thursday, October 8th, 9:40 AM. Call 937-555-0247 ext. 3 or e-mail handclinic@gemcityortho.example.org to change it. You may need surgery if the bone slips.
See your primary doctor, Dr. Bishop, within 2 weeks about your blood pressure.
Results and these instructions: https://mychart.riverbendmercy.org - activation code K7QX-29PL-M4.

COME BACK TO THE ER OR CALL 911 IF
* Fingers turn numb, white, blue or cold, or you cannot move them
* Pain keeps getting worse despite medicine, or the splint feels too tight
* Severe headache, repeated vomiting, confusion, new weakness, or you are very sleepy
* Fever, or redness or a bad smell from under the splint

Questions? Call the ED nurse line at (937) 555-0182, open 24/7.
Signed: W. Colles, MD | Patient signature: ____________

Patient: LÉVESQUE, Geneviève Thérèse ("Vivi")
Born 27 February 1934 - age 92
Ontario health card 5821-447-193-KT | Chart no. RVG-2209-6613
Visit 2026-10-11 (arrived 06:52, discharged 15:30)
Physicians: Dr. Jean-François Bélanger; Dr. Amrit Sandhu-Kaur (resident)
Family physician: Fiona Hodgkin, MD - Clinique Familiale Beechwood

Dear Madame Lévesque,

You came to us by ambulance this morning from Résidence Les Jardins Beauséjour (2245 Bearbrook Road, apt 314, Gloucester ON K1B 4N9). The staff found you more confused and weak than usual, and you had not been drinking much for about three days. Your daughter, Marie-Ève Ouellet-Lévesque, met you here and stayed with you all day.

What we found
Your blood tests show that you are dry (dehydrated): your kidney test (creatinine) was 142, up from 98 when it was checked on 2026-06-03. Your urine shows a bladder infection, which in older adults often causes confusion. Your chest x-ray and heart tracing were normal. Your blood pressure was low on arrival (102/58) and came up after 1 litre of IV fluid. You did not fall and you have no injuries.

By early afternoon you were back to your usual self - you were telling the nurses about your 41 years teaching piano at the École de musique Sainte-Cécile in Hull. You, your daughter and the team agreed you can go home safely with extra help from the residence.

Your medicines
- NEW: cephalexin 500 mg by mouth 4 times a day for 7 days. First dose given here at 13:10; next dose tonight at bedtime. Sent to Pharmacie Beausoleil (St-Laurent).
- STOP your water pill (hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg) until Dr. Hodgkin reviews your kidney test.
- Keep taking your other usual medicines.
- Drink 6 to 8 glasses (about 1.5 litres) of fluid a day. The residence nurse, Solange Picard-Ndiaye, has a copy of this plan.

About your Hodgkin lymphoma
Your record notes Hodgkin lymphoma treated with radiation in 1987, with no sign of it since. Nothing today suggests it has come back.

Follow-up
- See Dr. Hodgkin by Wednesday, Oct. 14 for a repeat creatinine and the urine culture result. Clinic: 613-555-0190, poste 4412.
- We will call your daughter at (613) 555-0127 if the culture means the antibiotic must change. Her e-mail on file: marieeve.ol@courrielsud.example.ca
- Your results online: www.rvgh-hgvr.example.ca/monportail

Come back right away or call 911 if
- you become confused or drowsy again, or cannot keep fluids down;
- you have a fever above 38.5 °C, shaking chills, or new pain in your back or side;
- you feel faint when standing, or you fall;
- you pass very little urine.

Non-urgent questions: Health811 (dial 811, 24/7).

Prepared by J.-F. Bélanger, MD
Copie remise à la patiente et à sa fille le 11 octobre 2026.
